questions.question: 一个人练了正念，能精准察觉「胸口发紧、在重播那句批评」，可每次都跟上一句「我怎么这么没出息」。按布拉克「两只翅膀」的说法，问题在哪？
options: 这是 RAIN 里正常的探究阶段，不需要做调整
正念还练得不够深，看得再清楚些自责就会消失
只有看清缺了慈悲，正念被用成了更精确的自我审判
只有慈悲缺了看清，他其实是在用笼统的自我安慰回避感受
questions.explanation: 只有看清没有慈悲，正念会变成冷冰冰的自我监控，看得越清骂得越准。缺看清的那一侧表现为笼统的「没事别想了」，与这个例子相反。
questions.question_en: Someone practicing mindfulness can precisely notice 'tight chest, replaying that criticism,' but always adds 'I'm so pathetic.' In Brach's 'two wings' image, what's wrong?
options_en: This is the normal Investigate stage of RAIN and needs no adjustment
Their mindfulness isn't deep enough; seeing more clearly will end the self-blame
Clear seeing without compassion: mindfulness has become sharper self-judgment
Compassion without clear seeing: they're using self-soothing to dodge feelings
questions.explanation_en: Clear seeing without compassion turns mindfulness into cold self-surveillance: the clearer you see, the more precisely you scold. Compassion without clear seeing looks like a vague 'it's fine, don't think about it,' the opposite of this case.

questions.question: 一个人身处一段伤害自己的关系，很害怕它结束。按布拉克对全然接受的界定，该怎么理解「接受」？
options: 先忍耐眼前的处境，等内心彻底平静、不再害怕之后再做任何决定
接受只适用于改变不了的事，关系能改变所以不适用
接受意味着先原谅对方，看见对方伤害背后同样的苦
接受的是自己的恐惧和痛苦这些内在体验，不等于要留在关系里
questions.explanation: 全然接受的对象是内在体验，而不是外在的一切行为和处境：接受「我害怕这段关系结束」不等于必须留在伤害你的关系里。「先忍耐」正是批评者担心的、把接受误用成忍耐。
questions.question_en: Someone is in a relationship that harms them and is terrified of it ending. Given how Brach defines radical acceptance, what does 'acceptance' mean here?
options_en: Enduring the situation until they feel completely calm, then deciding
Acceptance applies only to unchangeable things; relationships can change, so it doesn't apply
Accepting means first forgiving the partner by seeing the suffering behind the harm
Accepting their own fear and pain as inner experience, not agreeing to stay
questions.explanation_en: Radical acceptance targets inner experience, not every outer behavior or circumstance: accepting 'I'm afraid this will end' doesn't mean staying in a harmful relationship. 'Endure first' is precisely the misuse critics worry about, acceptance turned into putting up with it.

questions.question: RAIN 的 N 在 2003 年《全然接受》里是「不认同」，后来布拉克把它改成「滋养」。她给的理由是什么？
options: 不认同容易触发创伤者的闪回和解离，所以被整个删除
学员探究时常缺少温暖，直接谈不认同容易变成理智上的抽离
滋养这个词更好记，更便于把练习推广给普通大众
不认同与佛教的无我教义相冲突，因而遭到了不少传统老师的批评
questions.explanation: 她发现很多人在探究时缺少足够的温暖，直接谈不认同会变成抽离，于是单列「滋养」，把不认同视为做完四步后自然落入的状态——它被挪到后面，并没有被删除。
questions.question_en: In the 2003 Radical Acceptance, the N in RAIN stood for Non-identification; Brach later changed it to Nurture. What reason did she give?
options_en: Non-identification tended to trigger flashbacks in trauma survivors, so it was removed entirely
Students often lacked warmth while investigating, so non-identification became intellectual detachment
Nurture is easier to remember and makes the practice easier to popularize
Non-identification clashed with Buddhist no-self teachings and drew criticism from traditional teachers
questions.explanation_en: She found many people lacked enough warmth when investigating, so jumping to non-identification turned into detachment; she added Nurture and treated non-identification as the natural result after the four steps. It was moved, not deleted.
